title: Tile a Two-Row Floor With Dominoes and L-Pieces

concept.title: Split every tiling into blocks that cannot be cut by a vertical line
body: A floor has 2 rows and `n` columns. You have unlimited **dominoes** (2 cells, laid flat or standing) and **L-pieces** (3 cells, an L-shape in any of its 4 turns). In how many ways can the floor be covered exactly, with no overlap and no gap? For `n = 3` there are 5 ways, for `n = 4` there are 11. The answer is printed modulo 1 000 000 007.

Look at the **left end** of a tiling. Cut it by the first vertical line (between two columns) that no piece crosses; the part to the left of that line is a *block* that cannot be cut again, and the rest is any tiling of the remaining columns. How can a block that cannot be cut look? Width 1: one standing domino. Width 2: two flat dominoes (two standing ones would be two blocks of width 1). Width `k >= 3`: exactly **2** shapes, a chain of L-pieces that interlock (and the same chain mirrored).

body.code:
f[0] = 1
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    f[i] = f[i - 1]                       # a block of width 1
    if i >= 2: f[i] += f[i - 2]            # a block of width 2
    if i >= 3: f[i] += 2 * prefix[i - 3]   # a block of width k >= 3: 2 shapes, any tiling of the rest
    prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + f[i]       # prefix[i] = f[0] + ... + f[i]

body: Here `prefix[j]` is the sum `f[0] + ... + f[j]`, kept so that the sum over all block widths costs O(1). Check by hand: `f(2) = 2`, `f(3) = f(2) + f(1) + 2 * f(0) = 5`, `f(4) = 5 + 2 + 2 * (1 + 1) = 11`. The time is O(n). A neat formula `f(n) = 2 f(n - 1) + f(n - 3)` follows from the same table, but the block idea is what carries over to other tiling problems.

statement: A floor has 2 rows and `n` columns. You have unlimited dominoes (two joined cells, in either direction) and L-pieces (three cells, in any of the four turns). Print the number of ways to cover the floor exactly, modulo 1000000007.
outputFormat: Print one number: the number of tilings modulo 1000000007.

examples.note: Three standing dominoes; a flat pair and a standing one in two orders; two L-pieces in two ways: 5.

hints: Find the first vertical line that no piece crosses; what can the part to its left look like?
Widths 1 and 2 have one block each; every width of 3 or more has two blocks.
Keep prefix sums of f to add f over all widths at once.

explanation: Every tiling is a sequence of blocks that cannot be cut by a vertical line: one block of width 1, one of width 2, and two of every width 3 or more. So f(i) = f(i - 1) + f(i - 2) + 2 * (f(0) + ... + f(i - 3)), computed with prefix sums.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())

MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
f = [0] * (n + 1)
prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
f[0] = 1
prefix[0] = 1
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    total = f[i - 1]
    if i >= 2:
        total += f[i - 2]
    if i >= 3:
        total += 2 * prefix[i - 3]
    f[i] = total % MOD
    prefix[i] = (prefix[i - 1] + f[i]) % MOD
print(f[n])
